title: The well
hook: they drop him into a well, and Allah inspires him that one day he'll tell them what they did
carry: even in the well, a promise
tomorrow: The shirt and the false blood

segments.voice: Yesterday: hasad, the brothers' plan, jealousy with repentance already scheduled. Your line was jealousy makes plans. Did you catch one, and name it? Day fifty-seven.

The brothers have their plan. Now they need their father to let the boy go. So they go to Ya'qub, all warmth. Father, why don't you trust us with Yusuf? We only wish him well. Send him with us tomorrow. He'll run and play, and we'll look after him. And Ya'qub says something that should chill them. It grieves me that you'd take him away. And I'm afraid a wolf might eat him while you're not paying attention. A wolf. He's handed them the words. They answer: if a wolf eats him, with all of us there, we'd be losers indeed. And in the morning, the boy goes out with them. Today: the well.
screen: `FATHER, TRUST US WITH HIM.` → `I FEAR A WOLF.` → `HE GOES WITH THEM.`

segments.voice: Surah Yusuf, verse fifteen, and the Qur'an tells the worst moment in almost no words. So when they took him away, and agreed to put him in the depths of the well. That's it. No description of the struggle, the shouting, the boy's face. The Qur'an doesn't linger on the cruelty. It moves straight to what matters more. And We inspired him: you will surely tell them about this deed of theirs, while they do not realize. Picture where that promise lands. A boy, maybe still a child, at the bottom of a dark, damp well, his brothers' voices fading overhead. And into that darkness comes a message: this isn't the end. One day you'll stand in front of them and tell them what they did. It doesn't take him out of the well. It doesn't stop the caravan, or the slavery, or the prison that's coming. It gives him a thread to hold in the dark. Notice who the promise is for. Not the brothers; they don't hear it. Not Ya'qub; he's at home, waiting. Just Yusuf, alone, where nobody else can reach. The Arabic for the depths of the well is ghayabat al-jubb. Readers of the Arabic hear in ghayaba the root for what's hidden, unseen, the root of al-ghayb, the unseen world the Qur'an speaks of. The bottom of the well is the place where you vanish from sight. And that's exactly where the promise reaches him. Some years later, and a few days from now for us, we'll see it kept.
screen: `THE WORST, IN A FEW WORDS.` · `YOU WILL SURELY TELL THEM.` · `A THREAD TO HOLD IN THE DARK.` · `GHAYABAT — THE HIDDEN DEPTHS.` · then, large: `EVEN IN THE WELL, A PROMISE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit in a dark minute, not alone. If you can, close your eyes, or dim the light. Let the room get quiet. Think of the darkest place you've been, or are in now. You don't need to relive it. Just touch the edge of it. Then imagine that, even there, something reached you: a voice, a memory, a promise, a person. What was it? If nothing reached you then, imagine what you'd want to hear now. If you pray, you can remember that Allah reached Yusuf at the bottom of the well. The bell holds the time.
The well. Where Yusuf's brothers left him, and where a promise found him: one day you'll tell them what they did. Today's word.
Your line: even in the well, a promise. If you know someone in a dark place today, be the voice that reaches them: one message, one call. Day fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims often recite and reflect on Surah Yusuf in times of grief or hardship; the promise to Yusuf in the well is remembered as a sign that Allah reaches people where no one else can.

original.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:10 and 12:15: "the depths of the well" — from the root for hidden, unseen.

trapdoor: what you thought: brothers threw a boy down a well.
what it means: in the darkest moment, the Qur'an skips the cruelty and gives the boy a promise: one day you'll tell them.
what a scholar hears: ghayaba, the well's depths, shares the root gh-y-b with al-ghayb, the unseen; the place you vanish from sight is where the inspiration reaches him.

notes: 'Maybe still a child': the Qur'an doesn't give Yusuf's age; commentators give various ages. Stated with 'maybe'.
Whether the inspiration in 12:15 was prophetic revelation or inspiration (ilham) is discussed by commentators; the script says 'We inspired him' without deciding.
Trapdoor root link (ghayaba / al-ghayb, root gh-y-b): confirm.
Ya'qub's wolf line (12:13) and the brothers' reply (12:14) paraphrased.

Editor review 2026-10-01: 'and they won't even know who you are' read one commentary view into 'while they do not realize' (12:15), which commentators take more than one way; cut. The ghayaba / al-ghayb root note is now framed as what readers of the Arabic hear, not a stated etymology.
